thread:
acme_netops: Hey team — after migrating to an interface VPC endpoint for Redwood, our internal services intermittently get TLS/connection resets to the API. Public subnet can hit api.redwood.com fine; private subnets (same VPC) get: 
```
* About to connect() to api.redwood.com port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 10.10.4.23...
* Connected to 10.10.4.23 (10.10.4.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake started
* SSL read: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
* Connection reset by peer
```
Happens from multiple instances. Seen after we attached the interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-xxx). Any quick checks? :sos:
thread_continued:
matt_h: Thanks — quick checklist: can you paste the VPC endpoint ID, the subnet route table for the instances failing, and the endpoint security group? Also can you run a quick dig against the API hostname from the failing host (we want to see if it resolves to the endpoint IP or public IP).

matt_h: Quick repro commands to run from a failing instance:
```bash
# DNS resolution
dig +short api.redwood.com

# verbose curl to see TLS/SNI stuff
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.10.4.23

# openssl to inspect cert and SNI
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.4.23:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts
```

elaine_r: Also check that the VPC endpoint was created with Private DNS enabled (most frequent gotcha). If Private DNS is off, api.redwood.com will still resolve to public IPs and your traffic will hairpin out via NAT (or hit a different path) — leads to cert/SNI mismatches or resets. :eyes:
thread_more:
acme_netops: Pasted details:
- Endpoint: vpce-0abcde1234567890
- Endpoint SG: sg-0f1e2d3c4b5a6a7b8 (ingress tcp/443 from our subnets)
- Route tables for the affected subnets point to local (no custom routes)

Ran dig and curl results:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com
34.215.10.11

$ openssl s_client -connect 34.215.10.11:443 -servername api.redwood.com\CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3
---
no peer certificate
---
closed
```
So dig is returning a public IP (34.215.10.11) not 10.x private ENI. We didn't realise Private DNS was off.
thread_response:
sre_oncall: Bingo — that matches Private DNS being disabled. Two likely outcomes when that happens:
- Instances resolve to public IP and traffic goes via NAT/IGW; depending on outbound path and source IP filtering at our edge, the TLS flow can get reset.
- Or you hit a public LB that expects different SNI/cert, resulting in handshake failures.

Fix is to enable Private DNS for the endpoint (console: VPC > Endpoints > modify > enable Private DNS) or add a Route53 private hosted zone override. After enabling, do `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` or restart `systemd-resolved` and verify `dig +short api.redwood.com` returns the 10.x addresses (ENI IPs).
thread_resolution:
acme_netops: We enabled Private DNS on vpce-0abcde1234567890 and flushed resolvers. Now:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com
10.10.4.23
10.10.4.24

$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to 10.10.4.23 (10.10.4.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/2 200
{ "status": "ok" }
```
Looks stable for ~30m across hosts. :thumbsup:
thread_closure:
matt_h: Great — thanks for confirming. Notes for the ticket: root cause = Private DNS not enabled on AWS Interface Endpoint -> DNS resolved to public IP -> traffic hairpinned via NAT -> TLS resets. Remediation = enable Private DNS or add private hosted zone; verify `dig` resolves to endpoint ENI IPs.

elaine_r: Adding follow-ups (internal playbook links): https://redwood.internal/docs/vpc-endpoints#private-dns and checklist to avoid this during onboarding.

support_bot: Incident resolved and ticket marked as "customer actioned". :white_check_mark:
